column1: # The symbols of the X libraries h3maped was linked against, as the image's .dynsym records
# them; `homm3 loki link` generates its stub libXi, libXext and libX11 from this table
# (homm3.loki.xstubs), Red Hat 6.0's X libraries being lost (docs/loki/README.md, Link).
# Rows 6 to 203 are the image's .dynsym entries 6 to 203: the runs ld 2.9.1 added while it read
# libXi, libXext and libX11 (DT_NEEDED order; libdl's run is 1 to 5). ld enters a shared
# library's symbol in the output's .dynsym, in that library's .dynsym order, the first time a
# library names a symbol the program already references or defines, and copies a function's
# st_size from the library that defines it. XInput functions are libXi's, MIT-SHM and SHAPE
# ones libXext's, the rest Xlib's (libX11). libXi's run also holds XFree, and libXext's
# XGetVisualInfo and XIfEvent: Xlib functions those libraries call (undefined there). libXi's
# run holds _DYNAMIC, _init, _fini and _GLOBAL_OFFSET_TABLE_ too, which every ld-built library
# defines and the executable's own definitions override (st_size 0, the executable's type).
# A row named `symbol@VERSION` is an undefined versioned reference of the library to a glibc
# symbol. ld 2.9.1 enters such a reference in its hash table as `symbol@@VERSION`, the name
# under which glibc's definition is later entered, and allocates PLT slots in hash-table order
# (each bucket newest entry first): strrchr@@GLIBC_2.0 and _IO_link_in@@GLIBC_2.0 share a
# bucket, and the image gives _IO_link_in (286) the PLT slot before strrchr's (367), which
# needs strrchr@@GLIBC_2.0 entered before libc.so.6, whose .dynsym defines _IO_link_in first:
# by an X library (Red Hat's libX11 calls strrchr). No other reference is proven; the index
# is that of the symbol's own .dynsym entry.
#   index      the image's .dynsym index
#   symbol, type, size
#              the image's st_name (and version), st_info type and st_size
#   library    the library whose .dynsym names the symbol (whose run holds it)
#   defined    the library that defines it, which gives its st_size
# index
